title: Detailing a Barn Find That Sat for 22 Years
creator: Gus Pellegrino
description:
A 1980s coupe that hasn't seen soap since 2002. Full wash, decon, polish and interior.

This video is sponsored by Tollway roadside assistance. Use code GUS for your first month free at https://tollway.com

sentences.t: This car has not been washed since two thousand two, and today that changes.
Before we get the pressure washer out, this video is sponsored by Tollway.

Alright, let's take a walk around this thing.
It's a mid eighties coupe that a guy's grandfather parked in a barn and then just never drove again.
There's a solid layer of dust, some bird situations on the roof, and I'm pretty sure there's a mouse nest in the engine bay.
The paint underneath is a dark burgundy, I think, but right now it's mostly the color of a barn.
The good news is that dust actually protected the paint a bit from the sun.
Step one, I'm not touching it with a mitt yet, because all that grit would scratch the paint like sandpaper.
So it's a pre rinse with the pressure washer, a good distance back, just to knock the loose stuff off.
Look at the water coming off, that's like chocolate milk.
Next, snow foam, a nice thick layer over everything, and we let it dwell for five minutes so it softens the grime.
While that sits, I'm doing the wheels, which are honestly the scariest part.
Twenty two years of brake dust baked on, so this needs an iron remover.
Watch it turn purple as it reacts, that's the iron dissolving, very satisfying.
Okay, rinse off the foam, and now the two bucket wash, one bucket with soap, one with clean water for rinsing the mitt.
Top down, straight lines, no circles.
Oh wow, okay, it is definitely burgundy, look at this panel.
After the wash, a clay bar, because there's still contamination stuck in the clear coat that you can feel with your fingers.
You can hear it grabbing, and then as it gets clean it goes smooth and quiet.
Now for the polish, and I'm going one panel at a time with a dual action polisher.
I did a test spot on the hood first, and a single stage polish brought most of the gloss back.
There are a couple of deep scratches on the passenger door I'm not going to chase, because I don't want to burn through original paint.
Then a coat of sealant to protect it, because this car's going to start getting driven again.
Interior time, and I'm wearing a mask for this, you should too.
The seats are velour, which actually cleans up really well with an extractor.
The carpets came out three shades lighter, and I found a cassette tape under the seat.
It's a mixtape, handwritten, labeled summer eighty nine, and I'm giving it back to the owner, obviously.
Last step, the engine bay, which got a gentle degreaser and a lot of patience.
And yes, there was a mouse nest, it's been evicted, nobody was home.
So here it is, after about fourteen hours of work.
Same car, twenty two years later, and the paint looks like it could be from a showroom if you don't look too close.
The owner is picking it up tomorrow and I can't wait to see his face.
Let me know in the comments what barn find you want to see next.
Catch you in the next one.
